title: Conformance tests for selector v2: correctness across kernels + NaN/overflow guards
creator: Noah Patel
description:
Context
Selector v2 changes which attention/prefill/decode kernels get chosen as a function of model family, seq bucket, and GPU SKU. We’ve had historical incidents where a “fast” kernel was numerically unstable for a rare shape (overflow/NaN) or had a shape/stride assumption mismatch. Because selector v2 is intentionally more aggressive + explicit across SKUs, we need hard correctness gates that run continuously and cover the actual selection matrix.

Goal
Add conformance tests that validate numerical correctness for the kernel chosen by selector v2 across representative shapes and regimes (prefill vs decode; short vs long context), and add runtime NaN/overflow guards with a safe fallback kernel set.

Non-goals
- Proving bitwise equivalence across kernels (we’ll use tolerances).
- Full end-to-end model quality evals (handled by perf/evals pipeline); this is kernel-level/runtime-level conformance.

Acceptance criteria / Definition of Done
1) A new conformance test suite runs in CI and in benchmark-lab, exercising selector v2 decision paths across:
   - Model families: Llama-family, Mistral-family, Qwen-family (at minimum)
   - GPU SKUs: L4, A10, A100, H100 (or closest available in CI; benchmark-lab covers full matrix)
   - Seq buckets: short prefill, long prefill, steady-state decode (at minimum)
2) Each test executes the selector v2 “chosen kernel” AND a known-safe reference kernel for the same inputs and compares outputs within tolerance.
3) Tests include NaN/Inf detection and fail hard with a minimal reproduction payload (model family, kernel id, gpu sku, seq bucket, head dims, batch size, dtype, seed).
4) Runtime adds a guard path (feature-flagged) to detect NaNs/Infs post-kernel and automatically fall back to safe kernel set for that request (and emit a structured event/metric).
5) Unknown model families must use safe kernel set by default (covered by tests).
6) Documentation: add short “how to run conformance suite locally” instructions + how to interpret failures.

Proposed approach
A) Test harness
- Add a “kernel conformance harness” under runtime tests that can:
  - Construct representative attention shapes based on selector context (B, S_prompt, S_total, H, head_dim, n_kv_heads, dtype)
  - Invoke kernel via runtime interface (same codepath selector v2 uses)
  - Invoke reference kernel (safe baseline; slower but stable)
  - Compare outputs (and optionally intermediate stats) with tolerances
- Deterministic seeds and fixed random input distributions (normal(0,1) with clipping) to improve reproducibility.

B) Shape coverage
We will cover a small-but-representative matrix rather than an exhaustive cross product.
Initial matrix (subject to iteration after first failures):
- dtypes: fp16, bf16 (bf16 is mandatory on A100/H100; fp16 for L4/A10)
- head_dim: 64, 80, 128
- n_heads / n_kv_heads combos:
  - MHA: n_heads=32, n_kv_heads=32
  - GQA: n_heads=32, n_kv_heads=8 (common for Llama-ish variants)
- batch sizes: 1, 4, 16
- seq regimes:
  - Prefill short: prompt_len=128, total_len=128
  - Prefill long: prompt_len=4096, total_len=4096
  - Decode steady: prompt_len=2048, total_len=2049 (single step decode)
  - Decode long-context: prompt_len=8192, total_len=8193 (on SKUs that support it)

C) Tolerances / checks
- Primary: max_abs_error + relative error thresholds (per-output-tensor). Proposed defaults:
  - bf16: atol=2e-2, rtol=2e-2
  - fp16: atol=3e-2, rtol=3e-2
- Always fail if any NaN/Inf appears in output.
- Track error distribution (p50/p99) and log summary to test output for debugging.

D) Runtime NaN/overflow guard
- Add optional post-kernel validation:
  - fast path: check a sampled subset of output elements (configurable) for NaN/Inf
  - slow path (only when enabled): full tensor check
- On detection:
  - emit “kernel_conformance_nan_detected” event with selector context (bucketed) + kernel id
  - retry with safe kernel set (v1 safe kernel or explicitly curated safe kernels)
  - if retry also produces NaN/Inf, surface error (do not silently return)
- Guard must be feature-flagged and default-off for general fleet; we may enable in canary and Dedicated evaluations.

E) CI + benchmark-lab integration
- CI: run a minimal GPU subset (likely L4 or A10) with limited matrix to keep runtime manageable.
- Benchmark-lab: nightly/triggered runs across full GPU matrix and expanded seq lengths.
- Produce an artifact that maps (model_family, gpu, seq_bucket, kernel_id) -> pass/fail + any NaN events.

Implementation notes / open questions
- Reference kernel choice: we need a “known-safe” kernel that is available on all SKUs/dtypes we test. If we have a CPU fallback, it may be too slow; prefer GPU safe kernel even if slower.
- KV cache layout: ensure harness matches the same layout/stride assumptions as runtime to avoid false negatives.
- Some kernels may be non-deterministic across runs (e.g., atomic reductions). If observed, we will compare against reference within wider tolerance and/or compare summary stats; but NaNs/Infs remain hard fail.
- For very long-context cases on smaller SKUs (L4/A10), memory may be tight; we should skip long-context decode if it OOMs and explicitly mark as “not applicable” rather than failing the suite.

Links
- Design context: kernel-auto-selection v2 (Confluence)
- Related work:
  - ENG-3923 selector v2 core
  - ENG-3926 kernel registry schema
  - Slack thread: correctness concern (NaN) under specific shapes (eng-runtime)
- Expected code landing:
  - GitHub PR: pr_18501_conformance_tests_for_selected_kernels.json (target)

Rollout
- Gate selector v2 expansion on conformance suite passing in benchmark-lab for the relevant GPU cohorts.
- Enable NaN guard in internal canary + a small hosted cohort first; evaluate overhead and event rate.

Task breakdown
1) Build harness + reference kernel adapter (Anika)
2) Add initial shape matrix + family-specific metadata fixtures (Anika + Grace)
3) Add NaN/Inf detection + structured debug dumps (Anika)
4) Wire into CI with minimal GPU coverage; document how to run locally (Sahana + Anika)
5) Add benchmark-lab job definition + artifact export (Rina)
6) Review with kernel team + SRE for guard telemetry + failure modes (Grace, Allison)
comments: 2026-01-23 (Anika Gupta): Drafted test matrix proposal and sent to Grace/Yuki for review. Need confirmation on which kernel we consider “reference safe” across fp16/bf16 on L4/A10/A100/H100. Also want to confirm whether we need to include fused RMSNorm+attn paths here (my preference: no, keep it pure attention kernel conformance).

2026-01-27 (Grace Kim): Agree on scope: attention kernels only, no fused layernorm. For reference kernel, prefer `attn_flash_safe_v1` (slower but stable). For H100 we can still use it, even if not optimal. Please ensure harness forces same KV layout as runtime; we’ve had false mismatches previously when tests used contiguous KV but runtime uses paged KV.

2026-02-02 (Yuki Sato): Heads-up: A10 has a known edge case on head_dim=80 with one of the fast decode kernels; we saw sporadic NaNs in a profiling run (not yet pinned). Please prioritize covering (A10, decode steady, head_dim=80, GQA).

2026-02-06 (Anika Gupta): Implemented harness skeleton + deterministic seeding. Added output comparison with rtol/atol and NaN/Inf hard fail. Working through wiring so selector v2’s chosen kernel is invoked via the same API as production (no direct kernel calls).

2026-02-10 (Omar El-Sayed): Please include selector context dump in failure: selector_version, model_family, seq_bucket, gpu_sku_normalized, chosen_kernel_id, and override_source (none/registry/override/fallback). This will make triage in canary much faster.

2026-02-14 (Anika Gupta): Added failure dump (JSON blob in test logs) + reduced matrix for CI (batch {1,4}, head_dim {64,128}, seq {128 prefill, 2048+1 decode}). Full matrix remains for benchmark-lab. Open: long-context decode cases sometimes OOM on L4 in our CI runners; I’ll mark those as skipped with explicit reason.

2026-02-18 (Sahana Iyer): CI runtime budget is tight. Please keep GPU conformance job under ~12 minutes. Suggest running only fp16 in CI and leaving bf16 to benchmark-lab nightly. Also, we should avoid running all models; use family fixtures rather than full weights.

2026-02-20 (Anika Gupta): Pushed PR for conformance suite + NaN guard prototype behind `runtime.kernel_nan_guard.enabled`. Need review from Grace + Allison on event naming and whether we’re okay with sampling-based checks by default in canary.

2026-02-22 (Allison Grant): For telemetry, please follow cardinality standards: kernel_id is ok, but model name is not. Use model_family + seq_bucket + gpu_sku_normalized only. Also, NaN guard should emit a counter and a sampled structured log; don’t emit per-request spans for every success path.

2026-02-23 (Grace Kim): Reviewed PR; looks good. One requested change: make the “safe kernel set” explicit and versioned (do not implicitly call selector v1). We want deterministic behavior even if v1 changes. Marking this ticket In Review pending that change + green benchmark-lab run on A10 long decode.
